parsed.wine_summary:
Terroir Al Limit is the project of Dominik Huber, a Swiss-born winemaker who moved to Priorat in the early 2000s and built one of the most focused natural wine operations in the appellation. Where many Priorat producers blend Garnacha and Carignan for balance, Huber makes single-variety wines that interrogate what each grape can do on its own. Les Tosses is the Carignan statement — named for a specific parcel, farmed organically and biodynamically, and made with minimal intervention.

Carignan has a complicated reputation. It's high-acid, high-tannin, and historically used as a blending grape because it's difficult to ripen and easy to over-extract. What old vines on llicorella do to Carignan is the reason this wine exists: the slate forces deep root penetration, stress-limits yields naturally, and produces fruit with concentration and mineral tension that younger vines or richer soils can't replicate. Eight months in oak (for the 2022) is short enough to preserve the grape's structure without burying it in wood.
parsed.terroir_expression: Priorat's llicorella is decomposed black slate and mica schist — it drains aggressively, retains heat during the day, and radiates it back at night, creating the diurnal temperature swings that preserve acidity in a region that can push 40°C in summer. The slate's low organic content forces vines to root deeply, sometimes 10+ meters, pulling up trace minerals that show up as an iron and graphite note in the wine. Les Tosses sits at higher elevation within Priorat, which moderates the heat further and extends hang time — critical for Carignan, which needs time to shed its hard tannic edge. What you taste is the direct consequence of that geology: dark fruit, dried herbs, black olive, and a saline, almost metallic finish that no amount of winemaking technique can manufacture.
parsed.vinification_summary: Huber works with native yeasts and avoids additions, which means fermentation reflects whatever microbiological reality the vineyard delivers that year — a genuine risk that also produces wines with more textural variation than heavily managed fermentations. The 2022 sees eight months in oak, which for a wine of this structure is a seasoning tool rather than a flavor source; the goal is micro-oxygenation (slow oxygen exposure through the barrel staves) to soften Carignan's characteristically hard tannins without stripping the grape's natural acidity or mineral character. No fining, no filtration — the wine goes in the bottle with everything the vintage gave it. Biodynamic farming adds a layer of soil health management that, whatever your view on its metaphysical components, demonstrably produces lower yields and more complex root systems.
